findings.claim: Multiplier panel says there is no short proof to learn.
findings.evidence: This experiment is a solver run, not a proof-size lower bound. Beame and Liew construct polynomial regular-resolution proofs for degree2 identities on array multipliers; commutativity is one of their explicit cases. The local circuit is a shift-and-add array multiplier returning only low n product bits.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an empirical solver-search statement: dense bit interactions make short useful clauses difficult for this solver to find. Label low n product bits/modulo2^n, and preserve completed widths and measured conflict counts.

findings.claim: LLM-to-PDDL-to-planner pipeline promises a plan guaranteed to work.
findings.evidence: LLM+P §3 assumes a provided domain PDDL file and translates the problem/initial state/goal. The paper gives a generated PDDL example with invented predicate and omitted initial fact. Planner soundness is relative to encoded domain/problem; it does not certify natural-language translation or physical model fidelity.
findings.recommendation: Say a plan valid in the supplied formal model, conditional on faithful translation; show that the translation/model must be checked. Preserve historical PlanBench percentages.

findings.claim: MYCIN65% is labeled as percent of cases.
findings.evidence: Yu et al. evaluated10test cases using8independent expert evaluators. The reported65% is acceptability rating, while the five faculty specialist ratings were42.5–62.5%. It is not65% of10cases. Main comparative conclusion is supported.
findings.recommendation: Use acceptability rating65%, with10cases/8evaluators as context; do not present it as clinical efficacy or case success rate.

findings.claim: Recovered original code is immediately described as the ELIZA judged human23% in2025.
findings.evidence: Jones/Bergen §4.1 specifies a Python implementation of DOCTOR citing Brainerd2023. The recovered original program is a separate historical object. The23% result and5minute simultaneous three-party setup are verified.
findings.recommendation: Separate the claims explicitly: original reanimated in2024; a Python DOCTOR implementation was judged human23% in2025. Do not imply the recovered original was the tested implementation.

findings.claim: Recap says admissible A* examines a fraction of the space and alpha-beta searches twice as deep for the same work, unconditionally.
findings.evidence: An admissible h may be identically0, yielding uniform-cost search. Alpha-beta can approach minimax work under poor move ordering; the b^(d/2) benefit is the best case discussed correctly in the problem set.
findings.recommendation: Use A* can reduce search, and alpha-beta can reach roughly twice the depth with excellent move ordering. Keep the earlier exact best-case theorem.

findings.claim: Exercise6 parenthetical says correlated clusters inflate the expected number of satisfying assignments.
findings.evidence: The solution correctly derives E[X]=2^n(7/8)^m by linearity. Dependence between assignment indicators does not change that expectation. Correlations/uneven solution counts make the first-moment bound loose; they do not add an extra inflation to the derived mean. Main bound5.19 and refutation examples are correct.
findings.recommendation: Replace parenthetical with: the first moment is only an upper bound; a large expectation need not mean a formula is likely satisfiable, since solutions can be concentrated in a small fraction of formulas. Label4.267 as physics prediction rather than proved exact3SATthreshold.

findings.claim: Delete relaxation, a fast solution cost, h_max and FF-style extraction are presented as one easy-cost construction.
findings.evidence: An arbitrary relaxed plan can be found in polynomial time, but minimum relaxed-plan length h+ is NP-hard. h_max is a cheaper admissible fact-cost approximation. The local ff implementation chooses h_add-cost achievers and counts their union; original FF extracts from a relaxed planning graph. Existing wording can be interpreted charitably as finding any relaxed plan, so this is precision repair rather than demonstrated solver failure.
findings.recommendation: State that cheap approximations to delete relaxation guide search: h_max is admissible, while an FF-style extracted relaxed-plan length need not be. Label local heuristic FF-style unless exactly reproducing originalFF.

findings.claim: A Lean proof that compiles is called correct without assumptions.
findings.evidence: Lean accepts proofs relative to their statement, definitions and axioms. Compiling can succeed with sorry/custom axioms or unintended statement meaning; the official validation guide requires examining axioms and meaning. The actual1+1=2 toy statement itself is fine.
findings.recommendation: Say kernel-checked proof of the formal statement under its declared assumptions, with no unproved placeholders; relate semantic/formalization checking to the PDDL qualification.

findings.claim: Schank and Minsky are described as naming AI winter atAAAI1984.
findings.evidence: The actualAAAI84panel transcript lists DrewMcDermott, Waldrop, Schank, Chandrasekaran, JohnMcDermott, and DARPARonOhlander. DrewMcDermott introducesAIwinter as an already-used phrase. Minsky is mentioned as a participant in a different Asimov seminar. This does not prove no other1984warning byMinsky existed, but the directly available panel does not establish that attribution/coinage.
findings.recommendation: Safest source-backed wording: a1984AAAIpanel discussed a possibleAIwinter, with Schank warning about exaggerated expectations. Cite the1985published panel rather than assert coinage.

findings.claim: FirstUIP is a point every path passes through; every competitive solver is said to useCDCL.
findings.evidence: UIP quantifies paths from the most recent decision literal to the conflict; graph has other decision roots. The implementation docstring278–280 correctly describes current-level resolution. Competitive incomplete SAT solvers/portfolios need not all be pureCDCL.
findings.recommendation: Specify latest-decision-to-conflict paths and say leading complete general-purpose solvers commonly useCDCL. Current textbook implication graph hardcoded decisions appear internally consistent; completedcdclJSONabsent.

findings.claim: Modern gradient update is displayed inside a block labeled Samuel learning rule.
findings.evidence: Local implementation uses tanh(w·features), a differentiable semi-gradient update and bootstrapped search target. This is a Samuel-inspired modernTDanalogue, not a literal reconstruction of1959feature-correlation and replacement machinery. Publisher abstract verifies general learning claim but full1959primarytext was unavailable from attempted public academicPDF; exact historical-rule comparison remains reference-limited.
findings.recommendation: Label displayed gradient a modernTD-style analogue inspired bySamuel; preserve originaldelta/search idea and separate currentConnectFour experiment. Avoid treating this as a demonstrated learning bug.
